elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Rendered 12.4 now reads "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory." The term-plus-24-month prohibition ("Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory") is gone, and no other field-of-use or territory restriction binds Customer; retained 12.3 affirmatively confirms "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete ... commitment."

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: after the edit no competing-product restriction binds Customer at all, so the scope condition does not apply. The preferred outcome exceeds this fallback limit.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter" temporal anchor was removed with the prohibition; no in-term or post-term restriction remains.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the 24-month tail is deleted and no duration mechanic survives, so no duration cap is required.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied and expressly confirmed: 12.4 as rendered permits Customer to "develop ... any product or service that competes with Vendor," and 12.3 confirms nothing restricts Customer from developing any product or service.

Vacuously satisfied and expressly confirmed: rendered 12.4 permits Customer to "acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory"; 12.3 likewise preserves acquiring and licensing rights.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the sole preferred element is met in operative language, not merely promised in the margin comment. The fallback checklist is also satisfied vacuously because no restriction on Customer survives.

Classification as a deviation is correct: the original 12.4 was walk-away on two independent grounds — a 24-month post-term tail (>12 months) and undefined scope ("any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory") — so a redline rather than a rationale note was required.

Minimality holds: only the offending sentence in the second Section 12.4 was touched, the numbering and surrounding sections are retained, and no survival tail, expense, remedy, or procedural extras were added. The affirmative permission is the direct inverse of the deleted prohibition rather than a new requirement. Optional tightening (not a defect): because retained 12.3 already states that nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, or selling any product or service in any field or territory, striking 12.4 outright would avoid the mild operative redundancy.

Intent preserved: the edit removes a sentence that contradicted retained 12.3 and leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference; the no-hire restriction in the first Section 12.4 (p0045) is correctly left to the no-hire rule, avoiding double-flagging the same commercial term.

Margin comment complies with tone and playbook citation requirements — it states what changed, why, and offers the narrowed fallback (one named product, term only, \u226412 months, carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions) without lecturing.
